fix(cli): honor configured dashboard port without overriding explicit zero

LynCo-Patch: F33
Source: 795f80012036d4ed53533cf2378d2c20195a2b8f
Compared historical port publication 945b4ac0d5d31409eb52c0cb03d874726c0f5e90: selected implementation already in the donor; no duplicate import.

Route ordinary and supervised dashboard startup through the existing global setting before the default port. Explicit zero retains OS-assigned-port semantics. Bound the port range and reject malformed explicit input rather than silently binding an unrelated configured/default port. No new setting or operating controller.

Validation: upstream CLI has 6 failing routing cases/1 positive control; patched dispatcher and resolver pass all 101 tests on Linux/Node22.16.0. Does not start or reconfigure the live dashboard.

Delete-when: upstream's actual CLI honors absent/explicit-zero/explicit-valid precedence and rejects invalid explicit ports without reading a replacement setting.

replacements.new: | `daemonPort` | `number` | `4040` | Port for daemon/serve binding and the dashboard fallback listen port. `fn dashboard` and bare `fn` use this when no `--port`/`-p` flag is provided; the CLI flag wins for that launch. |
const explicitPort = pi !== -1 && args[pi + 1]?.trim() ? Number(args[pi + 1]) : pi !== -1 ? Number.NaN : undefined;

if (explicitPort !== undefined) throw new RangeError("Dashboard port must be an integer from 0 to 65535");
